title: How does a tray of mangoes grow when we add to it?
description: Mangoes sit packed in rows and columns on a market tray, drawn as a rectangle of dots. One more row is laid on, then one more column, and the video stops on how many new mangoes the tray gains.
teaching_notes: One idea: a total made of rows and columns grows by whole rows and whole columns. Collect guesses for the new mangoes and confirm none, because the chapter settles it. Watch for students who count only the new row and forget the new column.

source: A product is a rectangle of rows and columns
video_script.why: Before any rule, the child meets the chapter's question: when the numbers we multiply grow, how does the answer grow.
video_script.substitution: Picture the tray as a rectangle of dots in rows and columns, and watch a whole row and a whole column join it.
video_script.anchor: a market tray of mangoes packed in rows and columns, drawn as a rectangle of dots like the dot diagram of the book
hold_back: one row plus one column plus the corner
maths_rules: The tray is a rectangle of dots in rows and columns; no number of rows, columns or mangoes is said or shown.
One full new row and one full new column are laid on; how many new mangoes arrive is asked and never answered.
No symbols are drawn; the trays appear as pictures of mangoes and dots.
video_script.design: One idea: a total of rows and columns grows by whole rows and whole columns. Assumes counting in rows and columns. Wrong idea: none is broken. The tray stays to the end; no hard clear.
